chapters.title: Using Excel for Simple Data
chapters.content:
Welcome to Google Sheets Mastery!

Google Sheets is your online data powerhouse! In Book 1, you used calculators for math. Now, advance to organizing, calculating, and charting data like a pro, for projects such as festival toy tracking. Let’s dive in!

What is Google Sheets?

A free web tool for spreadsheets, accessible anywhere.

Why Learn More?

Analyze trends, like Eid spending, for smarter decisions.

Chapter Preview:

You’ll explore grids, organize data, use formulas, and create charts.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open sheets.google.com.

lessons.title: Introduction to Spreadsheets
lessons.content:
Spreadsheets are digital organizers for numbers and words! You’ll explore advanced features like merging cells and freezing panes to manage data efficiently, like inventory for festival toys. This builds on Book 2's file organization.

Why Focus on Grids?

They structure data for easy analysis.

Key Tips:

Use rows for items, columns for details; name ranges for quick reference.

Fun Fact: Google Sheets can handle over a million rows, powering global projects!

Class Activity Preview:

You’ll explore the grid next.

activities.title: Explore Google Sheets’ Grid
activities.introduction: Let’s build a structured grid! You’ll merge cells, freeze panes, and name ranges for a professional setup.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open sheets.google.com (with adult help).

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Click cell A1, type “Toy Inventory”; select A1:B1, Format > Merge cells > Merge all.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Freeze row 1: View > Freeze > 1 row.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Enter toy names in A2:A5; select A2:A5, Data > Named ranges, name “Toys”.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Name the sheet “MyFirstSheet” (File > Rename).

activities.challenge: Freeze column A and name B2:B5 “Counts”.

lessons.title: Entering and Organizing data
lessons.content:
Enter data like toy counts and organize with sorting, filtering and conditional formatting to spot patterns advancing from Book 2's file management.

What’s Organizing?

Sorting/filtering data, highlighting with colours for insights.

Key tip:

Use conditional rules for auto highlights , like green for high counts.

Fun fact: Conditonal formatting in sheets can change based on formulas, like traffic light for grades!

Class Activity Preview:

You’ll input and organize toy data next.

Parent Tip: Discuss data trends with your child !

activities.title: INPUT TOY CAR COUNTS
activities.introduction: Let's organize toy data dynamically! You will enter counts, sort,filter and format conditionally.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open sheets.google.com, create a new sheet.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: In A1-A5, list toys (e.g....car,doll,robot); B1-B5, counts(e.g...,5,3,7).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Select A1:B5, Data > Sort range > Sort by column B(Z to A).

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Add filter : Data > Create a filter, filter B>4.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Conditional format: select B1-B5 , Format > conditional formatting > Greater than 4 > Green fill.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.content: Name the sheet " Toy Cars ".

activities.challenge: Filters for even counts only.

activities.introduction: List 3 family events in column A, dates in B , costs in C, sort by cost , red format > 500 , name "Events".

lessons.title: Using simple Formulas
lessons.content:
Formulas calculate dynamically! Use SUMIF/AVERAGEIF for conditions and validations for accuracy , like summing specific Eid gifts_extending Book 2's Python inputs.

Why Formulas?

Automate math for quick insights.

Example: Average toys over a count threshold.

Funfact:

Sheet formulas update live, so changes ripple instantly _ like quick math!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll calculate gifts totals next.

DIY Idea: Track real festival expenses!

activities.title: Calculate Eid gifts Total
activities.introduction: Let’s make your presentation pop with sounds and videos! You’ll add an audio clip and a video to your slides, building on your animated slide.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open "ToyCars".

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: In B6, type "= SUMIF(B1:B5,">3")" for sum over 3.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: In B7,type"= AVERAGEIF(B1:B5,">3")" for average.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Select B1:B5, Data > Data validation > Number > Between 1-10 > Show warning.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Press Enter ; rename if needed.

activities.introduction: List 4 chores in A, hours in B , categories in C,SUMIF indoors, validate hours 1-5,name " Chores".

lessons.title: Creating Charts
lessons.content:
Charts visualize data professionally! Add trendlines, labels and customize for interactive insights, like festival food trends_ advancing from Book 2's Canva visuals.

What's a Chart?

Graphic data representation with trends.

Example: Bar chart with popularity line.

Fun fact: Sheet charts can be embedded in Docs, turning reports in visual!

Class Activity Preview:

you'll make a food chart next.

Parent Tip: Interpret chart trends together!

activities.title: Make a festival food chart
activities.introduction: Let's create an interactive Chart! You'll add data, generate a combo chart ,and customize.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open sheets.google.com and create a new sheet.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: In A1-A4, foods (e.g., Biryani, samosa); B1-B4, popularity (10,8); C1-C4,votes (20,15).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Select A1:C4, Insert > Chart > Combo chart( bar for B, line for C).

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: In chart editor , add trendline ( Series>trendline), data labels, axis titles(e.g.., " Foods " , "Scores" ).

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Name the sheet " Food Sheet ".

activities.challenge: Change to scatter plot with custom colors.

activities.introduction: List 3 cities in A, visits in B ,ratings in C , combo bar/ line chart with labels, name " Cities ".

lessons.title: Chapter 1 Summary and Final Home Activity
lessons.content:
You’re a Google sheet master! You:

1.1 - Explores grids with merging , freezing and ranges.

1.2 - Organized data via sorting, filtering and conditional formatting .

1.3 - Used conditional formulas and validations.

1.4 - Created customized interactive charts.

chapters.title: Advanced Scratch Animation
chapters.content:
Welcome to Advanced Scratch Animation Mastery!

Scratch (scratch.mit.edu) elevates your coding! From Book 2's basic Scratch Jr. advance to multi-scene, interactive animations with variables and clones for professional stories like Eid adventures. Let's code!

What is Advanced Scratch?

Block-based platform for dynamic projects.

Why Learn More?

Craft engaging narratives with user control.

Chapter Preview:

You'll build multi-scenes, add sound/motion, use loops/variables, create interactive tales.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open scratch.mit.edu.

lessons.title: Multi-Scene Animations in Scratch
lessons.content:
Multi-scenes create epic stories! Use backdrops and broadcasts for transitions, advancing Book 2's VEXcode paths to narrative flow, like switching festival settings.

Why Multi-Scenes?

Build layered tales with smooth changes.

Key Tip

Broadcast messages to sync sprites across scenes.

Fun Fact: Scratch's broadcast system mimics real-world signals, like radio waves in festivals!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll create a two-scene Eid story next.

activities.title: Create a Two-Scene Eid Story
activities.introduction: Let's craft a multi-scene narrative! You'll add backdrops and use broadcasts for transitions.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open scratch.mit.edu, click "Create".

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Stage Backdrops > Add two Eid-themed (e.g., home, mosque).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: In sprite script: "when green flag clicked (Events), "switch backdrop to Home" (Looks).

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Add "broadcast nextScene" (Events) after actions; "when I receive nextScene" switch to Mosque.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Name the project "Eid Story". (File>save)

activities.challenge: Add "wait 2 seconds" (Control) before broadcast.

activities.introduction: Add a third scene to "EidStory" with new broadcast, name updated project.

lessons.title: Adding Sound and Advanced Motion
lessons.content:
Enhance with custom sounds and motion paths! Import audio and use glide for realism, building on Book 2's Tynker sounds for immersive effects like festival drums.

What's Advanced Motion?

Precise paths with coordinates.

Key Tips:

Sync glide with sounds for timed effects.

Funfact:

Scratch's sound library includes global instruments, perfect for qawwali recreations!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll add music next.

Parent Tip: Record family sounds for projects!

activities.title: Add Festival Music to Story
activities.introduction: Let's make scenes lively! You'll import sound and code advanced motion.

lessons.title: Using Loops and Variables
lessons.content:
Loops repeat actions; variables track changes! Use for dynamic control, extending Book 2's Python loops to animation logic like varying kite speeds.

Why Loops/Variables?

Create efficient, adaptable code.

Key Tips:

Initialize variables before loops for control.

Funfact:

Variables in Scratch can be cloud-based, allowing shared projects across users!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll code a looping animation next.

DIY Idea: Experiment with variable displays!

activities.title: Code a Looping Kite Animation

lessons.title: Building an Interactive Story
lessons.content:
Make stories responsive! Use clicks, clones, and inputs for branching, advancing Book 2's Canva collaborations to user-driven narratives.

What's Interactivity?

Events triggering changes, like choices.

Key Tips:

Clones allow multiple instances with unique behaviors.

Funfact:

Scratch clones inspired game mechanics, like spawning enemies in adventures!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll make a clickable tale next.

Parent tip: Playtest stories together!

lessons.content:
You're a Scratch animation expert! You:

chapters.title: Mastering VEXcode VR for Complex Mazes
chapters.content:
Welcome to VEXcode VR Mastery!

VEXcode VR empowers virtual robot programming! Building on Book 2's obstacle courses, advance to navigating intricate mazes with precision, loops, and sensors for problem-solving challenges like exploring Pakistani landmarks. Let's program!

What is Complex Maze Programming?

Coding robots to solve multi-path puzzles efficiently.

Why Learn More?

Develop logical thinking for real-world robotics

Chapter Preview:

You'll build multi-scenes, add sound/motion, use loops/variables, create interactive tales.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open vr.vex.com.

lessons.title: Maze Programming Basics
lessons.content:
Maze basics involve planning paths with commands! Use Drivetrain blocks for initial navigation, advancing Book 2's simple courses to strategic planning, like a Lahore Fort layout

Why Maze Basics?

Establish foundations for complex problem-solving.

Key Tip

Map tums before coding: test incrementally.

Fun Fact: VEXcode VR simulates real robots used in global competitions!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll code a simple path next.

activities.title: Code a Simple Maze Path
activities.introduction: Let's start with fundamentals! You'll program a robot through a basic maze using motion blocks

lessons.title: Advanced Turns and Movements
lessons.content:
Refine movements with angles and speeds! Program precise turns and variable drivetrain for agility, extending Book 2's sensor avoidance to detailed control.

What's Advanced Movement?

Custom angles and velocities for tight spaces,

Key Tips:

Use "set drive velocity to 50%" for slower, accurate turns.

Funfact:

Real VEX robots compete in mazes at events like the VEX World Championship!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll program turns next.

Parent Tip: Discuss robot paths like a game strategy!

Why Loops?

Reduce blocks for scalable paths, like repeating tums.

Key Tips:

Nest motions inside loops; adjust counts for patterns.

Funfact:

Loops in coding mimic real robot assembly lines in factories!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll use loops for moves next.

Layered code for decision-making paths.

Use "if" with sensors inside loops for adaptability.

VEXcode VR mazes train skills for autonomous drones in exploration!

chapters.title: Mastering Python for Simple Games
chapters.content:
Welcome to Python Game Mastery!

Python transforms your coding into interactive adventures! Building on Book 2's Python basics, advance to creating text-based games with conditions, variables, and loops, like guessing games inspired by Pakistani culture. Let's code!

What is Python Game Coding?

Writing programs for interactive challenges.

Why Learn More?

Build fun, logical games to share with friends.

Chapter Preview:

You'll master conditions, variables/inputs, loops, and game creation.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open colab.google.com

lessons.title: Conditions in Python
lessons.content:
Conditions make programs decide! Use "if" statements to check answers, extending Book 2's Scratch events for game logic, like quizzing about Pakistani landmarks. Compare to Scratch (Book 3, Ch. 2) for cross-tool leaming.

Why Conditions?

Enable choices, like right/wrong quiz answers.

Key Tip

Use"" for exact matches; indent code under "if".

Fun Fact: Python's "if" logic powers AI assistants like me!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll code a quiz question next.

activities.title: Code an "If" Quiz Question
activities.introduction: Let's create a decision-making quiz! You'll use conditions to check answers, similar to Scratch's event blocks.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open colab.google.com, create a new notebook.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Type: answer input("What is Pakistan's capital?").

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content:
Add: if answer "Islamabad:
print("Correct!").

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Add: else: print("Oops, it's Islamabad!").

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Run cell, test answer, name notebook "QuizGame".

activities.challenge: Add a second question about a festival (e.g. Eid).

activities.introduction: Write a yes/no question (e.g., "Is Lahore a city?"); name "YesNoQuiz".

lessons.title: Combining Variables and Input
lessons.content:
Variables store game data, like player names! Combine with inputs for personalization, building on Book 2's input basics and Scratch variables (Book 3, Ch. 2).

Why Variables/Input?

Make games unique, like greeting players.

Key Tips:

Store inputs in variables; use"+" to combine strings.

Funfact:

Python variables can hold millions of values, like game scores!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll store a player's name next.

Parent Tip: Enter your name in your child's game!

activities.introduction: Code input for favorite city, print greeting, name "City Quiz"

lessons.title: Loops in Python
lessons.content:
Loops repeat actions for engaging games! Use "while" loops to retry questions, advancing Book 2's Scratch loops and linking to Scratch's repeat blocks (Book 3, Ch. 2).

Why Loops?

Keep games running until a condition is met.

Key Tips:

Use "while True" for continuous loops; "break" to exit.

Funfact:

Loops in Python run apps like music playlists on repeat!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll loop a question next.

DIY Idea: Count loops in real life, like festival songs!

activities.title: Loop a Question Three Times

lessons.title: Creating a Text Game
lessons.content:
Combine skills for a full game! Build a guessing game with conditions, variables, and loops, extending Book 2's Scratch games to Python text adventures.

What's a Text Game?

Interactive program with challenges, like guessing numbers.

Key Tips:

Combine "if", variables, loops for dynamic play.

Funfact:

Python games inspired classics like text-based adventure Zork!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll build a number game next

Parent tip: Play the game together!

activities.title: Build a Number-Guessing Game

lessons.title: Chapter 4 Summary and Final Home Activity
lessons.content:
You're a Python game master! You:

4.1 - Coded conditions for quiz logic.

4.2 - Used variables and inputs for personalization

4.3 - Added loops for repeated actions.

4.4 - Built a full text-based game.

chapters.title: Mastering AI Tools for Creative Projects
chapters.content:
Welcome to AI Tools Mastery!

Artificial Intelligence tools enhance productivity and creativity! Building on Book 2's AI image and audio creation, advance to using AI for drafting, editing, generating visuals, and assembling projects like applications and presentations. Focus on ethical assistance to support learning. Let's innovate!

What are AI Tools?

Systems that generate drafts, images, and ideas to aid tasks.

Why Learn More?

Boost efficiency in writing, visualizing, and presenting while practicing originality.

Chapter Preview:

You'll master conditions, variables/inputs, loops, and game creation.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open chat.openai.com, docs.google.com, or Slides.google.com

lessons.title: Using AI to Draft Applications
lessons.content:
AI like ChatGPT can generate initial drafts! Prompt for a school leave application, then review for accuracy, practicing ethical use by editing personally.

Why Draft with AI?

Get structured starting points to learn formatting

Key Tip

Provide clear prompts, always revise for your voice.

Fun Fact: AI drafting tools process requests in seconds, based on vast training datal

Class Activity Preview:

You'll draft a leave application next

Parent tip: Guide prompt refinement for better results!

activities.introduction: Let's use AI as a helper! You'll prompt for a draft application and discuss editing ethics

lessons.title: Editing AI Drafts in Google Docs
lessons.content:
Move AI drafts to Google Docs for refinement! Edit structure, add details, and format, focusing on learning writing skills through practice.

What's Editing in Docs?

Polishing content for clarity and professionalism.

Key Tips:

Use bold for headings; check spelling with built-in tools.

Funfact:

Google Docs tracks changes, showing edits like a digital red pen!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll edit an application next.

Parent Tip: Compare before/after versions!

chapters.title: Basic Coding and Movements with M3D GO
chapters.content:
Dive into M3D GO Coding!

Building upon the foundational setup established in the Chapter 12 Book 2, this section introduces the principles of coding movements using the Scratch interface integrated with M3D GO. You will learn to apply block-based commands to direct the robot's actions and exploration of motion concepts. This progression enhances computational thinking and prepares for more complex interactions in subsequent chapters.

What is Coding in This Context?

The process of assembling instructional blocks to control robot behavior, such as directing paths or adjusting velocities.

Why Focus on Movements?

Mastery of basic motions forms the basis for advanced applications, including navigation and task automation.

Chapter Preview:

Coverage includes introductory movement blocks, speed modifications, and sequence construction with integrated effects.

Instructions:

Confirm the robot is connected via Scratch before proceeding.

lessons.title: Introduction to Movement Blocks
lessons.content:
The Scratch environment provides specialized blocks for M3D GO, enabling precise control over the robot's locomotion. These include commands for forward and backward motion, as well as rotational adjustments. Understanding these blocks allows for the creation of deliberate trajectories, akin to mapping routes in a logistical system.

Why Begin with These Blocks?

They establish core functionality, ensuring reliable execution before incorporating variables.

Key Tip

Align blocks vertically to form logical sequences; test incrementally to verify outcomes.

Fun Fact: Block-based coding, as used here, aligns with educational methodologies employed in Pakistani STEM curricula to promote logical reasoning.

Class Activity Preview:

The subsequent activity involves applying these blocks for initial motion tests.

Parent tip: Ensure safe handling of robot parts!

activities.title: Basic Robot Movements
activities.introduction: This activity introduces the application of fundamental movement blocks, enabling users to observe direct responses from the robot.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open https://scratch.markhor3d.com/ In the Scratch workspace, locate the M3D GO extension blocks and drag the "When Green Flag Clicked" starter.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Attach the "Go Forward" block and execute the code to observe linear motion.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Add a "Turn Left" block following the initial command, then run the sequence to assess directional change.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Repeat with "Go Backward" to evaluate reverse functionality.

activities.challenge: Construct a sequence resulting in a 180-degree rotation using turn blocks

activities.introduction: Reproduce the class sequence at home, executing forward and turn commands.

lessons.title: Adding Speed and Controls
lessons.content:
Enhancing movement involves modulating velocity through percentage-based parameters and incorporating alternative input methods, such as keyboard controls. This allows for nuanced adjustments, optimizing performance for specific tasks.

Why Incorporate Speed?

Variable speeds enable simulation of real-world dynamics, improving precision in applications.

Key Tips:

Utilize lower percentages for controlled maneuvers and higher for efficient traversal.

Class Activity Preview:

The activity explores these enhancements through targeted testing

activities.title: Control Speed and Direction

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Modify the "Go Forward" block to "Go Forward at 30%" and observe the reduced velocity.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Increase to "Go Forward at 70%" and compare traversal times over a fixed distance.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Use arrow keys to direct motion while varying speeds via blocks.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Test a combined sequence, such as slow forward followed by a rapid turn.

activities.challenge: Determine the optimal speed for a curved path without deviation.

activities.introduction: Implement a sequence with alternating speeds, using keyboard inputs for real-time adjustments.

lessons.title: Simple Sequences with Effects
lessons.content:

Why Use Sequences?

Key Tips:

Employ "Wait" blocks to synchronize actions, ensuring coherent execution.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Execute and refine the timing for seamless flow.

activities.challenge: Extend the sequence to form a closed loop pattern with repeated turns

activities.introduction: Enhance a Sequence Construct a sequence incorporating at least three movements and one effect, such as a display message. Test variations and note improvements in execution. Sequence Enhancements: Introduce minor modifications, like alternating effects, to explore variability.

chapters.title: Level-Up Your AI with Google Teachable Machine
chapters.content:
Welcome to Advanced AI!

You've already taught an AI to recognize simple things! In this book, you'll become an AI expert by learning how to make your AI even smarter and more useful. We’ll dive into advanced techniques like teaching AI to understand your body, making it guess better, and even showing how it could be used in a real project!

What is Advanced AI?

It’s about making your AI models more accurate and teaching them to do more complex tasks.

Why Learn More?

To create amazing projects that solve real problems, like a plant that knows when it needs water!

Chapter Preview:

You’ll train an AI to recognize complex poses, fix its mistakes, and plan a real-world AI invention.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to open Teachable Machine, just like you did before!

lessons.title: Making AI Smarter (Dealing with Bias)
lessons.content:
Sometimes AI makes a mistake because it wasn't given enough good examples! This is called "bias." To make a smart AI, you need to give it lots of different examples. You also need to teach it what things are not the answer, using a "Background" class. This helps your AI focus on what's important, like learning how to spot different kinds of kites in a busy sky!

What is Bias?

.When an AI guesses wrong because its examples were all too similar.

Key Tips:

Take pictures from different angles and in different light. Add a "Background" class with no objects in it.

Fun Fact: Self-driving cars use AI trained on millions of images to see the road!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll train a smarter AI next.

activities.title: Train a Smarter AI
activities.introduction: Let’s train an AI that’s really good at telling the difference between things! You’ll collect lots of examples, including a "Background" class, to make your model super smart.

steps.title: Open Teachable Machine
steps.content: Go to the website and select "Image Project."

steps.title: Create Your Classes
steps.content: Rename "Class 1" to "Apple" and "Class 2" to "Orange." Add a third class and rename it "Background."

steps.title: Collect Examples
steps.content: For "Apple," hold an apple and use your webcam to take at least 30 pictures from different angles. For "Orange," do the same with an orange. For "Background," point the webcam at an empty table or a blank wall and take 20 pictures.

steps.title: Train and Test
steps.content: Click "Train Model" and wait. In the "Preview" window, show your AI an apple, an orange, and the empty table. See how well it guesses!

steps.title: Save
steps.content: Download your model and save it as "FruitAI.tm."

activities.challenge: Find an object that is neither an apple nor an orange (like a banana). Show it to your AI. What does it guess?

activities.introduction: Train a smarter AI to recognize a family member's face. Collect many pictures of their face, and also collect pictures of an empty room as the "Background" class.

lessons.title: Training AI with Body Movements (Pose Models)
lessons.content:
AI isn't just for pictures and sounds—it can also be a dance partner! With a Pose Model, you can train an AI to recognize your body's movements and gestures. Each pose is a different class, and the AI learns from the positions of your shoulders, elbows, and hands! This is just like learning the precise movements for a folk dance!

What is a Pose Model?

t’s an AI that learns to recognize the shape of your body in different positions.

Key Tips:

Make sure your webcam can see your whole body. Give lots of examples for each pose.

Class Activity Preview:

You’ll train an AI to recognize a secret hand gesture.

Parent Tip: Get your family involved! Everyone can help create new poses for the AI to learn.

activities.title: Train a Pose Model
activities.introduction: Let's teach an AI a secret move! You'll train a Pose Model to recognize two different body poses, which is a great first step toward making a game that reacts to your body!

steps.title: Open Teachable Machine
steps.content: Go to the website and select "Pose Project."

steps.title: Create Your Classes
steps.content: Rename "Class 1" to "Arms Up" and "Class 2" to "Arms Down." Add a third class called "Background."

steps.title: Collect Examples
steps.content: For "Arms Up," stand back from your computer and hold your arms up in the air. Use the webcam to take at least 30 pictures. For "Arms Down," put your arms down by your sides and take another 30 pictures. For "Background," step away from the computer so the webcam only sees an empty scene and record 20 pictures.

steps.title: Train and Test
steps.content: Click "Train Model." When it's done, stand in front of the webcam and raise or lower your arms. Watch how the AI guesses!

activities.challenge:
Add a third class called "Superhero
Pose" and train your AI to recognize it!

activities.introduction: Train a Pose Model to recognize a simple hand gesture, like a "thumbs up" or a "high five."

lessons.title: Improving Your AI Model
lessons.content:
What do you do if your AI makes a mistake? Don't worry, you can fix it! You can make your AI better by adding more examples, or by removing bad ones. This is called fine-tuning, and it's what real AI developers do all the time. It's like a chef tasting a dish and adding a pinch of salt to make it perfect!

How to Fine-Tune?

Add more examples to the class that the AI is guessing wrong. Delete pictures that are blurry or confusing for the AI.

Class Activity Preview:

You'll fix a buggy AI next.

DIY Idea: :Find a family photo that's blurry. Imagine how an AI might get confused trying to recognize who is in the picture!

activities.title: Fix a Buggy AI
activities.introduction: Let’s be AI detectives and fix an AI that is making mistakes! You’ll fine-tune an existing model to make it more accurate.

steps.title: Open Your Project
steps.content: Go to Teachable Machine and open your "FruitAI.tm" project.

steps.title: Make a Mistake
steps.content: Find a different kind of fruit (like a pear) that your AI might get wrong. Show it to your AI. What does it guess?

steps.title: 1.Add More Examples
steps.content: If the AI guessed "Apple" or "Orange," then it got confused. Let's make it smarter! Create a new class called "Other Fruit." Take 20 pictures of the pear and other random fruits for this new class.

steps.title: Re-Train and Test
steps.content: Click "Train Model" again. This will update your AI. Now, show the pear to the AI again. It should now be able to recognize it as "Other Fruit"!

activities.challenge: Try to find a blurry picture of an apple. If your AI guesses wrong, delete the blurry pictures from your "Apple" class, and then re-train the model.

lessons.title: Planning and Using an Advanced AI Project
lessons.content:
Now it's time to become a full-on AI project designer! You’ve learned how to train a smarter AI and fix its mistakes. Now you can use these skills to plan a more advanced and useful project. You’ll think about how to use your AI in a real-world setting, like a smart light or a game.

What is an Advanced Project?

An AI that solves a problem or makes something new possible, like an AI that helps you water a plant.

Example: An AI that turns a light on when it sees your face, but only after sunset!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll build a 5-step plan for your own advanced AI invention.

Parent Tip: Talk with your child about how AI could help with chores or everyday tasks around the house!

activities.title: Plan Your Advanced AI Invention
activities.introduction: Let's use all your skills to plan an amazing AI invention! You’ll think through every step of your project, from the idea to the final result.

steps.title: Open a Document
steps.content: Grab a piece of paper or open a blank document on your computer.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Step 1: The Goal! What's your project? Example: An AI that helps sort trash for recycling.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Step 2: The Training! How will you train your AI? What classes will you use? Example: I will use Image Model and collect pictures for "Plastic," "Paper," and "Metal" classes. I will also add a "Background" class.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Step 3: The Testing! How will you test your AI to make sure it's smart enough? Example: I will show it new trash items it has never seen before to see if it guesses right.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content:
Step 4: The Improvement! What will you do if your AI makes mistakes? Example:
If it guesses wrong, I will collect more pictures of that kind of trash and re-train it.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.content: Step 5: The Fun Result! How would your AI be used? Example: I would connect it to a small robot that pushes the trash into the correct recycling bin!

steps.content: Save your plan as "MyAdvancedAIPlan.txt."

lessons.content:
You're a Certified AI Architect! You have:

11.1 - Learned how to create a smarter AI by dealing with bias.

11.2 - Trained an AI to understand your body movements with a Pose Model.

11.3 - Learned how to fine-tune and fix a buggy AI.

11.4 - Planned an advanced AI project from start to finish.

Tell them to do one of the poses. If the AI guesses correctly, they get a point! If the AI guesses wrong, ask your family member to try a different angle, and then you try to fine-tune the model to make it better for next time!

chapters.title: Building Live Automations with n8n
chapters.content:
Welcome to Real-World Automation!

You've learned the secrets of automation: triggers, actions, and workflows! In this book, you’ll take the next step and build a real, working automation. You'll use n8n's visual builder to connect different apps and make them work together on their own, just like a smart factory!

What is a Live Automation?

It’s an automation that runs by itself on a computer somewhere, so you don't have to think about it!

Why Learn to Build Them?

To create powerful automations that save you time and make things easier, like getting an automatic weather report every morning.

Chapter Preview:

You’ll use the n8n website to build a real workflow, connect to real apps, and add smart decisions to your automations.

Instructions:

Ask an adult to help you create a free n8n Cloud account so you can build your own workflows. This requires a parent's email.

lessons.title: Your First Live Workflow (Trigger and Action)
lessons.content:
The first step to building a live automation is to make a simple, working chain with a Trigger and an Action. You’ll build a workflow that starts on a schedule (the Trigger) and does a simple task (the Action). You'll see your first real automation come to life!

What is a Schedule Trigger?

t’s an automation that starts at a specific time, like every day at 8 AM.

Key Tips:

Use Always start a new workflow with a Trigger node. Make sure your Action node is connected to the Trigger with a line.

Fun Fact: NASA uses automation to get reports from its space missions!

Class Activity Preview:

uses You'll build a workflow that sends a simple message to you.

activities.title: Build Your First Live Workflow
activities.introduction: Let’s build a workflow that sends you a message with a fun fact every day! You'll use a Schedule Trigger and a Set node to create your first working automation.

steps.title: Log into n8n
steps.content: With an adult's help, open the n8n Cloud website and log into your account.

steps.title: Start a New Workflow
steps.content: Click the "Create Workflow" button on the left.

steps.title: Add a Trigger
steps.content: Click the "+" button to add a new node. Search for "Schedule Trigger" and click on it.

steps.title: Set the Schedule
steps.content: In the node's settings, choose a simple schedule, like "Hourly" or "Every 5 minutes" so you can see it work quickly.

steps.title: Add the Action
steps.content: Click the small circle on the right side of the Schedule Trigger node to add a new node. Search for "Set" and add that node.

steps.title: Add a Message
steps.content: Inside the "Set" node's settings, click "Add Value." For the name, type "Message," and for the value, type "Hello from my first n8n workflow!"

steps.title: Run the Workflow
steps.content: Click "Save" and then turn on the workflow with the switch in the top right corner. Wait a few minutes, and you'll see a green checkmark showing it ran!

activities.challenge: Change the message to be a joke or a fun fact about AI!

activities.introduction: With an adult, build a workflow that sends a message with the date and time every morning at 8 AM.

lessons.title: Connecting to a Real App (Integration)
lessons.content:
Now for the real magic! n8n can connect to hundreds of different apps and online tools. We call this an integration. You can connect your workflow to a messaging app like Telegram, so your automation can actually send you a message on your phone!

What is an Integration?

AI It's when a workflow is able to connect to and use another app.

Key Tips:

You Integrations often need a special key (called an API key) that an adult can help you find. You have to choose the right Action node for the app you want to use.

Fun Fact: n8n has integrations for over 400 different apps!

Class Activity Preview:

You'll build a workflow that sends a real message to you.!

activities.title: Send a Real Message!
activities.introduction: Let’s connect our workflow to a real app and send a live message to your phone. We'll use the Telegram app, with a little help from an adult to get set up!

steps.title: Log into n8n
steps.content: Open your n8n account and start a new workflow.

steps.title: Add Your Trigger
steps.content: Add a "Schedule Trigger" node and set it to run "Hourly."

steps.title: Add a Set Node
steps.content: Add a "Set" node and, just like before, add a value with the message you want to send.

steps.title: Add the Telegram Node
steps.content: Click the circle to add a new node, search for "Telegram," and select the "Telegram" node.

steps.title: Connect Your Account
steps.content: With an adult's help, connect your Telegram account by getting the "Bot API Key" and the "Chat ID." This is the part that lets n8n talk to your phone!

steps.title: Send the Message
steps.content: In the Telegram node, select the "Chat ID" you got and then use the "Expression" button to pull the message from your "Set" node.

steps.title: Run and Test
steps.content: Click "Save" and turn the workflow on. Wait for the scheduled time, and you should see the message pop up on your phone!

activities.challenge: Change the message in your "Set" node to send a new joke or fun fact!

activities.introduction: With an adult's help, build a new workflow that sends you a message every evening at 6 PM saying, "Time for family dinner!"

lessons.title: Adding Smart Decisions (If/Then Logic)
lessons.content:
What if you want your automation to be extra smart? You can add an If node, which lets your workflow make a decision. The workflow can follow different paths based on a condition you set. This is called conditional logic! It's like a path that splits: "IF it is sunny, THEN go left, ELSE go right."

What is an If Node?

It's a special node that checks if a condition is true or false.

Key Tips:

The If node has a "True" branch and a "False" branch. You can check for things like numbers (is this number bigger than that one?) or text (does this message say "Hello"?)

Class Activity Preview:

You'll add an If node to your automation to make it smarter.

DIY Idea: Think of a rule you follow every day. For example, "IF it's a school day, THEN I go to bed at 9 PM." This is conditional logic!

activities.title: Make Your Automation Smarter
activities.introduction: Let’s add a smart decision to your workflow! You'll build a workflow that only sends a message if the temperature is hot!

steps.title: Log into n8n
steps.content: Open a new workflow.

steps.title: Add a Trigger
steps.content: Add a "Schedule Trigger" and set it to run every hour.

steps.title: Get the Weather
steps.content: Click the circle to add a new node. Search for "OpenWeatherMap" and add it. With an adult's help, get a free API key and set the city to your city.

steps.title: Add the If Node
steps.content: Add a new node after the OpenWeatherMap node. Search for "If" and add it.

steps.title: Set the Condition
steps.content: In the "If" node's settings, write your condition. For example, check if the temperature is greater than 25.

steps.title: Add an Action
steps.content: On the "True" branch of the If node (the top branch), add a "Set" node and write the message, "It's a hot day!"

steps.title: Run and Test
steps.content: Save and turn on the workflow. If it's a hot day, you'll see a green checkmark on the "True" branch! If not, the "False" branch will light up.

activities.challenge: Add a "Set" node to the "False" branch with the message, "It's a cool day!"

lessons.title: Planning Your Advanced Automation Project
lessons.content:
You're ready to plan a full-on automation! You know how to build workflows, connect to apps, and add smart decisions. Now, you’ll plan a project that uses all these skills to solve a real problem or do something amazing, like a smart shopping list or a homework reminder system!

What is an Advanced Project?

An automation that uses multiple steps, apps, and decisions to make a complex task easy.

Example: An automation that checks the weather, and if it's going to rain, sends you a message to bring an umbrella!

Class Activity Preview:

You’ll build a 5-step plan for your own advanced automation.

Parent Tip: Discuss your child's automation plan and help them think through all the steps and connections!

Get Ready:

activities.title: Plan Your Advanced Automation Invention
activities.introduction: Let's use all your skills to plan an amazing automation invention! You’ll think through every step of your project, from the idea to the final result.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: Open a blank document (like Google Docs or a simple text editor) or grab a piece of paper and a pencil.

steps.title: Open a Document
steps.content: Grab a piece of paper or open a blank document on your computer.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Step 2: The Goal! What's your automation? Example: An automation that tells me if I need to take a jacket to school.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.content: Step 3: The Trigger! What starts your automation? Example: A schedule trigger set to run every morning at 7 AM.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.content: Step 4: The Connections! What apps will your automation connect to? Example: I will connect to a weather app to get the temperature, and to a messaging app to send a message.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.content: Step 5: The Smart Decision! What decision will your automation make? Example: It will use an "If" node to check if the temperature is less than 15 degrees.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.content: Step 6: The End Result! What is the final action? Example: If the temperature is low, it will send a message that says, "Don't forget your jacket!"

lessons.content:
You're a Certified Automation Architect! You have:

12.1 - Built your first live workflow with a trigger and action.

12.2 - Connected your workflow to a real app using an integration.

12.3 - Added smart decisions using an "If" node.

12.4 - Planned an advanced automation project from start to finish.
